A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–H are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original bandit experiments using MovieLens 25M and Goodreads, plus synthetic experiments and an asymmetric-PE comparison in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 4 and Appendices A and C.

M1.justification: PE, PE-CS, asymmetric-PE, and FT-UCB retain the same procedures and pseudocode. The added feasibility assumption in Appendix H does not change the algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MovieLens 25M and Goodreads tasks and synthetic bandit scenarios, including reference-arm and subsidy sweeps and the appendix examples.

E2.justification: The comparator sets are unchanged: PE versus UCB-CS Known ℓ, and PE-CS versus ETC-CS, UCB-CS, and TS-CS. Membership within the main and appendix comparisons is retained.

E3.justification: Both versions retain the same rating normalization, genre-based arms, random costs, regret metrics, evaluation horizons, parameter sweeps, and ETC-CS exploration-budget specification.

E4.justification: Appendix A retains the synthetic sensitivity experiment, cost–quality trade-off plots, and UCB-CS failure example. Appendix C retains the same asymmetric-PE comparison.

E5.justification: The reported 25 independent runs in Figure 1 and 50 runs in Figure 2 and the toy experiment are unchanged. No uncertainty-reporting or statistical estimation procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: The plotted results, numerical instance specifications, and reported findings are unchanged across Figures 1–9 and their accompanying discussion. No result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: Before Theorem H.1, v2 explicitly assumes that at least one arm satisfies the fixed reward threshold. v1 defined the optimal feasible arm without stating this existence condition. The bounds and proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions retain the same proposed settings, logarithmic regret guarantees, PE order-optimality claim, characterization of PE-CS optimality, and empirical performance and reliability claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H newly explains that feasibility is ensured by the reference-arm and subsidized-best-reward settings but must be assumed for the fixed-threshold setting. This clarifies an applicability condition; existing result interpretations and optimality limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 4 adds a code-repository pointer in footnote 2, absent from v1. This improves documented access information; the PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or accessibility.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior cost-subsidy bandits, conservative bandits, and Improved-UCB remain unchanged. Removing a redundant local attribution does not remove the cited work or change that positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and capitalization edits, including replacing ambiguous references to the 'optimal arm' with 'best reward arm' in related work. It also updates acknowledgments and adds publication headers without reorganizing the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds ICLR 2025 headers and slightly reflows text, theorem openings, and footnotes. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–2 retain their content and presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves precision by stating the fixed-threshold feasibility assumption in Appendix H and improves reproducibility guidance through the Section 4 code pointer. These are useful clarifications, while the methods, proofs, and empirical evidence remain essentially unchanged.
